2026-10-07 L6 load-peers (mechanism of the slowdown with N; measured, no code changed). W6a on hbox, load 12-17, tmpfs, developer image native-c3-0b4d3b183 (fn-host-developer, core sha256 5e342d19...), preset peers (the test PROFILE), A and B on one box, 16G scope. 1,000: 28.7 and 33.2 articles/s excl node start, round=done (reproduces the 29.2/s). 10,000: round=failed reason=round-deadline at 600 s with imported=9013 and 8810 (two runs, 13.2 and 13.6 articles/s overall; the third round, begun at once, finishes the rest; divergence 0, chain digest equal). Per-1000 split seconds (run 2): 29.4 40.0 54.4 54.3 64.4 80.4 84.8 105.1 111.1 113.0, i.e. per-article time grows ~4x from the first to the tenth thousand, ~linearly in the count B holds. CPU seconds per 1000 articles by process/thread: A (serving) flat 22-26 s throughout; B pull worker thread flat 3.6 -> 5.3 s; B main sbcl thread 3.5 -> 20.6 s; B owner io thread 1.0 -> 34.1 s; B process total 14 -> 156 s per 1000. GC on B per 1000: 1,489 -> 18,808 collections and 2.6 -> 33.7 s of GC, dynamic usage after GC 528 -> 743 MiB. So the growth is B's owner-side work per imported article (commit/state path under the IHAVE the pull worker offers), allocating more per article as the store grows; it is not the pull worker's scheduling, the round driver, A's XFNCATCHUP serve, or the 10 ms poll. sb-sprof flat windows of B (w6-prof.lisp, 120 s each, window 0 = first ~4000 articles vs windows 1-3) show the same functions at stable shares with growing sample volume (19k -> 35k per 120 s): FN-CEI-BRANCH-GET (6.7 -> 8.7% total), FN-CROW$C-PGET (3.8 -> 6.1%), REVAPPEND, FN-CBOR-AG-CAR, FLOOR; so a persistent-structure lookup/copy cost per import that scales with state size, which the flat profile does not pin to one caller. The 600 s deadline (fn-prd-round-deadline) only turns this into a failed-then-resumed round; the cure is in the per-import owner cost, not the deadline. title: Catch-up import runs at about 1.3 articles a second (peer_catchup imports ~780 of 1000 in a 600 s round on hbox): the pull worker ends a selection at every spool, local, send and digest step (about 25 worker hand-offs an ~2 KiB article, 32 of them 64-octet digest reads), reads only the selection's last action as progress, and pauses ACL2's 10 ms I/O poll on the owner commit signal, which neither a spool worker nor a local submission raises; every selection also re-reads both plan tables under the owner
